item_verdicts.goal: the goal is a crew command that retires a sub-floor review dimension through record_dimension_disposition instead of a hand edit, and reckon/cli.py:3892 defines crew dispose with its write at reckon/cli.py:3960, its pointer-less revision resolution at reckon/cli.py:3793 and the corrected floor comment at reckon/crew/review.py:1169, so the operator retires the row by command and the entry lands in the file the row is read from.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records seven arms under arms/ and each claim I checked holds — arms/after_suite_promoted_run.log ends 53 passed EXIT=0 at 13e1fe70 with reckon.__file__ and review.__file__ naming that worktree, arms/baseline_suite.log ends 8 failed/40 passed EXIT=1 with ids exactly the new module's command cases, arms/pre_promoted_run_repair.log ends 2 failed/51 passed EXIT=1 failing exactly the pointer-less pair, and arms/negative_control_promoted_run.log ends 2 failed/51 passed EXIT=1 on the two unknown-kind cases.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared paths are reckon/cli.py, reckon/crew/review.py, tests/test_sub_floor_disposition_has_a_writer.py, the fragment and the figures directory, and git diff --stat 5636e306 6426a2cd lists exactly those six files and no other, with the last two commits touching only the fragment and its figure.

justifications.durability: the pointer-less pair reddens at 041be0b1 and the mutation control reddens exactly the closed-set pair, so both halves are load-bearing rather than covered by a case that would pass either way, but the command's own stored-is-None branch at reckon/cli.py:3943 has no case.
justifications.evidence: the seven arms under arms/ each open with the revision, the tree, the command and the imported module's path, and the base arm's eight failing ids are exactly the new module's command cases while the head arm ends 53 passed EXIT=0; the negative control's first line repeats the declared mutation with the repaired revision named inside it rather than contiguously, which the promotion check admits because it reads the failing ids and the exit status rather than the wording.
justifications.fit: the subcommand follows the neighbouring crew commands and resolves a run's tree and head through the same recovery helpers the obligations reader uses (reckon/crew/obligations.py:306), with no name the repository naming rules forbid.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/cli.py:3960 records the entry through record_dimension_disposition and :3971 re-reads it, so the receipt repeats what the store holds rather than what the call intended, and every refusal is the store's own; a call naming a dimension that carries no sub-floor row is accepted and reported ok, so the one thing the command exists to change — the row — is confirmed only by the operator's next obligations read.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 5636e306 6426a2cd lists only the declared paths, and the two refusals for a field belonging to the other kind and the pointer-less resolution answer defects an earlier review of this run named rather than new scope.
